name: Reel
text: Assign the Decisions Lead to own the Decision Ledger and enforce the one-sentence irreversible call rule with a 24-hour time-boxed veto. Neutrality stops teams from gaming Product’s sprint flow, and the time box forces urgency without paralysis. The trade-off is that some calls may get rejected or delayed, but the Board stays clean and decisions are actually irreversible.

name: Scriv
text: The time-boxed veto still lets teams game the system by weaponizing delay—half-baked calls pile up until the Lead’s veto window closes, then they force the call through as "irreversible." Instead, give the Decisions Lead a *preemptive gate*: every Board entry must include a one-sentence irreversible consequence *before* it’s logged, or it’s rejected outright. That settles it—no gaming, no paralysis, just enforced rigor.

name: Chisel
text: Assign the Decisions Lead to own the Decision Ledger and enforce the one-sentence irreversible call rule, with a time-boxed veto power: if they deem an entry half-baked, they must reject it within 24 hours or it auto-approves. This keeps neutrality while preventing paralysis, because the veto is time-bound, not endless. The trade-off is occasional rushed approvals when the Lead misjudges, but it stops teams from gaming the system by dumping half-baked calls to force a ruling.

name: Sift
text: The time-boxed veto still lets teams game the system by forcing the Lead into a binary choice: accept a half-baked call or slow the sprint. The real risk is paralysis—teams will flood the Ledger with borderline calls knowing the Lead’s veto is the only blocker. Settle it by making the Ledger entries *publicly reversible* for 48 hours after the sprint, with the Decisions Lead only certifying calls that survive that window.

name: Scope
text: Assign the Decisions Lead to own the Decision Ledger and enforce a *strict 24-hour validation window* for every "irreversible" call. They’re neutral, so teams can’t game Product’s sprint flow by dumping half-baked calls—if the Lead rejects an entry, it dies unless resubmitted with a stronger one-sentence consequence. The trade-off is a slight delay in Board decisions, but it forces clarity upfront and keeps the Ledger clean.
